title: One identity vocabulary for gold, adapters, and docs
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want one subject-key and label vocabulary shared by gold, adapters, scorer, and docs, so that corpus recall measures the scanner instead of the alias table.

## Current mess

Three vocabularies coexist:

1. **Corpus gold** (29 packets): mentions/PII keys are taxonomy (`pii:email_address`, `pii:national_identifier`, `pii:person_name`) with gold labels like `person_name` / `national_identifier`. Data-item keys are source fields (`data_item:uid`, `data_item:social_security_number`).
2. **Scanner findings**: `mention:${ruleId}`, `raw_hit:${ruleId}`, `data_item:${ruleId}` from `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml` (e.g. `email`, `ssn`) and rule labels (`user_email`, `social_security_number`).
3. **Written contract** (`tests/eval/ground-truth-schema.md`): still says exact `mention:${conceptId}` with `conceptId === ruleId`.

`tests/eval/identity.ts` maps (1) onto (2) with equivalence groups (email ≡ email_address ≡ user_email; ssn ≡ social_security_number ≡ national_identifier) plus parent/child label rules (`person_name` satisfied by `first_name`). Fixture Jest cases already use scanner identities, so they never exercise this bridge.

## Why it blocks scanner work

If we optimize the matcher so an alias group lights up, recall goes up and we will think the engine improved. Gold and the engine may still disagree on what a “social security number” *is*. Conversely, a real matcher improvement that emits the gold taxonomy would look like a regression if we later delete aliases without rewriting gold.

`national_identifier` sitting in the same equivalence group as `ssn` is an example of a policy choice, not a fact. Driver-license gold often shares the `pii:national_identifier` key and relies on `subject.name` to disambiguate. That is too easy to get wrong under identity-only data-item matching.

## Questions to answer

- Canonical keys: gold taxonomy, matcher rule ids, or adapters that translate findings into gold shape so the scorer stays exact?
- Canonical labels: gold taxonomy parents, matcher rule labels, or a published map with no fuzzy groups?
- Do we rewrite 1.8k gold keys, change adapters, or keep a *minimal* explicit map (not open-ended token groups)?
- What happens to fixture cases (`mention:email`) after the decision?
- How do docs, `normalizeSubjectKey`, and Plexus identities stay in lockstep?

## Not this task

Do not retune PII regexes to chase alias matches. Do not silently rewrite gold in this design task.

comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## Measured: how much of PII recall the alias table is actually carrying

Scored every gold key on the mentions and data-item layers against the 15 rule ids in `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml`, applying the `EQUIVALENCE_GROUPS` table from `identity.ts`.

| layer | cases | exact rule id | **alias-only** | no rule at any name |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mentions (`pii_signals`) | 357 | 30 (8%) | **213 (60%)** | 114 (32%) |
| data items | 436 | 81 (19%) | 47 (11%) | **308 (71%)** |

So the concern in the description is real and quantified: **60% of mention recall exists only because of `identity.ts`**, and 8% is honest exact identity. Delete the alias table without rewriting gold and mention recall falls to roughly an eighth of what it reads today.

### The part the task does not yet account for: a hard ceiling underneath

There are only 15 rules (`account_number, address, date_of_birth, drivers_license, email, first_name, full_name, last_name, national_id, passport, password, phone_number, ssn, tax_id, username`). The 114 + 308 cases in the right-hand column match **no rule under any alias**. They are unreachable regardless of which vocabulary wins.

Top unreachable mention concepts — these are real, and there is simply no rule:

- `access_token` x39
- `credential_secret` x29
- `password_verifier` x13
- `payment_card_data` x6
- `employment_information` x5, `city` x5, `compensation` x4, `residence_information` x3

Data items are unreachable for a different reason: gold was keyed on **raw source field names**, not concepts — `id` x17, `name` x8, `token` x7, `location` x5, `city` x5, `status` x3, `key` x3, `uid` x3, `pass` x3, `uuid` x3, `card_reference` x3.

Ceiling with today's rule set, assuming a perfect matcher: **~68% mention recall, ~29% data-item recall.**

That reframes the question. Whichever vocabulary is canonical, the report has to distinguish:

1. a rule exists and the detector missed it — a scanner problem;
2. no rule exists for this concept — a taxonomy-coverage problem;
3. a rule exists but gold named it something the map does not reach — a vocabulary problem.

Today all three land in the same recall denominator as "miss". Any flywheel started from that number sends the next session writing regexes for `uid` and `status`.

### A third bridge nobody has listed

`identity.ts` is not the only translation layer. `assertCanonicalSubjectKey` in `tests/benchmark/manifest.ts` **hard-codes** a `pii:` escape hatch:

```ts
if (canonical === "mentions" && (key.startsWith("mention:") || key.startsWith("pii:"))) {
  return;
}
```

on top of the `pii_signal:` -> `mention:` / `raw_hit:` migration in `normalizeSubjectKey`. So the vocabularies are bridged in two places, in different files, with different rules. All 357 mention annotations use `pii:` and reach the scorer only through this loader exemption. Whatever the decision, it has to name `manifest.ts` as well as `identity.ts` and the docs.

### On `national_identifier` specifically

The description flags this as a policy choice rather than a fact, and the data supports the worry: `national_identifier` appears 8 times in mention gold and sits in the same equivalence group as `ssn`, while `PARENT_TO_CHILDREN` also expands it to `drivers_license`, `passport` and `tax_id`. With data-items matched identity-only (no span check), a single `data_item:ssn` finding anywhere in the repo satisfies a driver-licence gold case in a different file. That is not a hypothetical; it is how `findingMatchesCase` short-circuits for `IDENTITY_ONLY_LAYERS`.

### Suggested shape of the decision

Recommend **adapters translate findings into gold shape, gold keys stay canonical**, with a closed published map and no open-ended token groups — but the decision is not usable until it is paired with a rule-coverage answer for the 422 unreachable cases (extend the rules, mark them `documentedGap`, or drop them from the denominator with a named reason). Picking a canonical vocabulary while 24% of the corpus has no detector concept at all just relocates the dishonesty.

Note for whoever picks this up: fixture Jest cases use `mention:email` style keys, so they never exercise either bridge. Whatever changes here, the fixture cases will stay green and tell you nothing. See KDATAP-89d1a6.

comments.text:
## Measurements supporting the decision, and one instruction it needs

### What the alias table is currently carrying

Scored every mention and data-item gold key against the 15 rule ids in `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml`, applying `EQUIVALENCE_GROUPS`:

| layer | cases | exact rule id | alias-only | no rule at any name |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mentions | 357 | 30 (8%) | **213 (60%)** | 114 (32%) |
| data items | 436 | 81 (19%) | 47 (11%) | **308 (71%)** |

So removing open-ended equivalence groups is not a tidy-up — 60% of today's mention recall exists only because of them. Expect the number to fall hard, correctly, on the first canonical run.

### There is a second rescue path, and it is bigger than the alias table

`conceptTokensForCase` in `identity.ts` also feeds `subject.name` into matching. **339 of 357 mention cases (95%)** carry a `subject.name` that differs from the key rest. So most mention cases today have two independent ways to match, and the decision closes both.

But those names are not display names. They are the **source token the annotator actually saw**:

| gold key (inferred concept) | `subject.name` (source token) |
| --- | --- |
| `pii:access_token` | `id_token` |
| `pii:user_identifier` | `sub` |
| `pii:credential_secret` | `refresh_token` |
| `pii:user_identifier` | `external_identifier` |
| `pii:email_address` | `clientID` |

This is exactly the separation the decision calls for on data items — "source names such as `uid` are separate from inferred concepts such as user identifier". Mention gold already records both; the source name is just sitting in the wrong field.

**Request: the migration should promote mention `subject.name` into the canonical source-name field, not discard it as a display name.** "Never an identity input" is right for matching and should stand. But a blanket drop destroys the only record of what was observed on 339 annotations, and it is the field that makes the remaining adjudication possible — `pii:email_address` named `clientID` is very likely a mislabel, and it is only visible because the source token was kept.

The rule needs to be per layer. On data flows, all 436 names are genuine prose restatements of the key ("OIDC callback to session") and should be discarded. On components, see KDATAP-08a0ac.

### A closed one-to-one leaf map cannot create leaves

Agreed that a curated adapter maps a detector rule id to one canonical leaf, closed and versioned. The constraint that follows: **422 of 793** mention and data-item cases have no detector concept to map to, at any name.

Unreachable mention concepts: `access_token` x39, `credential_secret` x29, `password_verifier` x13, `payment_card_data` x6, `employment_information` x5, `city` x5, `compensation` x4.

Unreachable data items are unreachable for a different reason — 308 of 436 are **source field names**, not concepts: `id` x17, `name` x8, `token` x7, `location` x5, `city` x5, `status` x3, `key` x3, `uid` x3, `uuid` x3, `card_reference` x3. Under this decision each needs a concept leaf assigned or an explicit "no concept" adjudication. That is the largest single block of human work in the epic.

Ceilings with today's rule set, perfect matching assumed: **~68% mention recall, ~29% data-item recall.**

Raised on the epic: these are eligible (file read) and permanently missed (no rule), which no eligibility reason currently describes. Proposing a reported `reachable` denominator as a diagnostic — not an exclusion, so raw recall still includes the miss.

### Two migration surfaces, not one

The `pii_signals` -> `mentions` rename is the layer name. Separately, `assertCanonicalSubjectKey` in `tests/benchmark/manifest.ts` **hard-codes** an exemption permitting `pii:` subject keys on the mentions layer:

```ts
if (canonical === "mentions" && (key.startsWith("mention:") || key.startsWith("pii:"))) {
  return;
}
```

All 357 mention annotations use `pii:` keys and reach the scorer only through it. The one-way migration and removal milestone need to cover the key prefix as well as the layer name, or the warning loader will be removed while the exemption quietly stays.

### On parent/child

Agreed and the data supports the concern. `national_identifier` appears 8 times in mention gold; `PARENT_TO_CHILDREN` expands it to `drivers_license`, `passport` and `tax_id`, and `EQUIVALENCE_GROUPS` puts `national_identifier` in the same group as `ssn`. With data items matched identity-only today, one `data_item:ssn` finding satisfies a driver-licence case in a different file. Separating exact-leaf from ancestor-category correctness fixes the reporting; the one-to-one rule on KDATAP-89d1a6 fixes the double credit.
